title: Dohākoṣa-nāma-caryāgīti of Saraha (the 'King Dohā')
alt_titles: do ha mdzod ces bya ba spyod pa'i glu (Tibetan)

structure.description: the Derge Tibetan (Tōh 2263) prepared as 40 four-line stanzas

summary: The song Saraha sang to the king: the one innate appears as many like waves on water; the true bliss is near like honey in one's mouth yet not drunk; mind free of stain is untouched by saṃsāra and nirvāṇa.

title: Mahāmudropadeśa of Tilopa (the Gaṅgā Mahāmudrā)
alt_titles: phyag rgya chen po'i man ngag (Tibetan)

structure.description: the Derge Tibetan (Tōh 2303) prepared as 29 four-line stanzas

summary: Tilopa's mahāmudrā instruction to Nāropa on the bank of the Gaṅgā: mahāmudrā cannot be shown, yet leave the mind uncontrived like space; clouds dissolve in space, thoughts in seeing one's mind; the kings of view, meditation, conduct and fruit; practice as a river from torrent to ocean; seek a skilled guru.

title: Dohākoṣa of Tilopa
summary: Tilopa's Treasury of Songs: the aggregates, elements and senses arise from and dissolve into the innate; do not worship Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva or go to bathing places; the four moments and four joys; the innate is known in the moment between the supreme joy and the joy of cessation.

editions.name: Derge Tengyur, Tōh 2281 (confirmed in the local Derge catalogue)

notes: Translated (colophon) by Vairocanavajra of Kosala; read locally.

title: Ṣaḍdharmopadeśa of Tilopa
summary: Tilopa's 'Instruction on the Six Dharmas': caṇḍālī (from Caryāpa), illusory body and clear light (from Nāgārjuna), dream (from Lavapa), the intermediate state and transference (from Sukhasiddhi) — the Indian root of the Six Yogas of Nāropa; translated by Nāropa and Marpa.

title: Caryāgīti (Caryāpada / Caryācaryāviniścaya)

structure.description: about fifty songs; in Shastri's manuscript songs 24, 25 and 48 and the end of 23 are missing and known only from the Tibetan (recalled, not checked)

summary: About fifty songs in Old Bengali (Apabhraṃśa-like Eastern vernacular) by some two dozen siddhas (Lūipa, Kukkuripa, Virūpa, Bhusuku, Kāṇha, Saraha, Śabara, Ḍombi, Śānti and others), each set to a rāga and signed by its poet, in intentional language about the innate and the yoga of the channels; with Munidatta's Sanskrit commentary.

title: Caturaśītisiddhapravṛtti (the Lives of the Eighty-four Siddhas)
alt_titles: grub thob brgyad cu rtsa bzhi'i lo rgyus (Tibetan)
summary: Abhayadatta's lives of the eighty-four siddhas, each a short narrative of a person of any caste or trade who met a guru, received an instruction suited to his or her life, practised (often twelve years) and attained mahāmudrā, with a verse of realization; preserved in Tibetan (translated by sMon grub shes rab).
notes: Not found in the local Derge Tengyur (it is in the Peking/Narthang Tengyur per memory). The unit's siddha entries use the closely parallel list and songs of Tōh 2292.

title: Caturaśītisiddhabodhihṛdaya (the realization songs of the eighty-four)
alt_titles: grub thob brgyad cu rtsa bzhi'i rtogs pa'i snying po (Tibetan)
summary: A collection of the realization songs of the eighty-four siddhas, in almost the same order as Abhayadatta's lives, each introduced 'from the mouth of guru X'; compiled by the master Vīraprabhāsvara (dpa' bo 'od gsal).
